name: Passenger Flow
description: The station catchment simulation: who wants to travel, from where to where, and when. It owns demand generation per station from catchment size and time of day — rush hours ride world.day_night_cycle's dawn and dusk rather than a private clock, so passenger pressure and the visible sky never disagree — and the queues that build when a route's capacity falls short of its catchment. Schedules changing (world.routeScheduleUpdated) re-aims demand immediately, because a passenger's loyalty is to the timetable, not to the company. Fares are collected on delivery by economy.currency and capacity is the vehicle's manifest; this component only produces the crowd and its patience. Overcrowding is announced as world.stationOvercrowded for the score and advisory layers — it never penalizes by itself, since a tycoon game teaches through lost revenue, not through fines the player did not choose.

inputs.name: baseDemandPerStation
inputs.description: Passengers wanting travel per station per game hour before multipliers. Sets the baseline a single-bus route can serve.

inputs.name: rushHourMultiplier
inputs.description: Demand multiplier during dawn and dusk rush windows. The spike is what makes fleet sizing a peak-versus-average tradeoff.

inputs.name: catchmentRadiusTiles
inputs.description: Tiles around a station that feed its demand. Overlapping catchments make station placement a territorial decision.

inputs.name: patienceSeconds
inputs.description: How long a queued passenger waits before giving up. Lost patience is lost fare revenue — the flow's only teeth, and they are economic.

outputs.name: waitingPassengers
outputs.description: Station id to queue length. The platform crowd UI and the overcrowding check both read this.

outputs.name: servedPassengersPerHour
outputs.description: Throughput actually delivered, the denominator of every load-factor conversation.
